metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3–7 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model delays correction; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 2–5 days.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods when sentiment is mixed or neutral; add 1–3% upward bias for 3–7 day horizon if sentiment shows upward momentum.
- If model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction of 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong downward trend after a spike, model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 5–10 days if sentiment remains negative.
